title: A raw rational Cauchy bound on two CReal samples lifts to a CReal closeness bound
statement: If the n-th rational samples of x and y are within k/(n+1) of each other (the raw, Rat-level Within predicate), then x and y are close as CReal values, within rate 1+(k+1) applied at n: |x - y| <= ofRat(natDivSucc (1+(k+1)) n). The rate absorbs k's own slack plus one unit of self-approximation gap for EACH of x and y (via the private one_sided_via_samples helper, called once per direction), fused by two applications of Rat.natDivSucc_add. This is the Within -> close_within bridge, generic in both x and y (stronger than any single caller needs: neither side is assumed to be a bespoke construction).

formal.statement: theorem CReal.close_within_of_within : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : CReal.Within (Rat.sub (CReal.seq x0 x2) (CReal.seq x1 x2)) (Rat.natDivSucc x3 x2)) -> CReal.le (CReal.abs (CReal.add x0 (CReal.neg x1))) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.add (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) (AxNat.add x3 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) x2)))))))
